clue.text: Machinist works to rule at first

parts.note: operas are musical works, the plural of opus

indicators.note: at first asks for only the opening letter of the word rule

explanation.surface: A factory hand stages a work-to-rule protest at the start of a dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Works to rule' reads as industrial action; 'at first' takes only the opening letter of rule. Opera is the plural of opus, a musical work.
explanation.definitionFit: A machinist is someone who works a machine, a synonym for a machine worker.

clue.text: A heavenly model

parts.note: read not as a gorgeous fashion model but as a clockwork model of the heavens, showing planets circling the sun

explanation.surface: Someone praises a beautiful fashion model.
explanation.definitionFit: An orrery is a mechanical model of the solar system, so literally a model of the heavens.

clue.text: Game in the form of a puzzle

indicators.note: a new form of the letters means they are rearranged into another shape

explanation.surface: A game is presented as a brainteaser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the form of' rearranges the six letters of GAME IN.
explanation.definitionFit: An enigma is a mystery or riddle, a synonym for something puzzling.

clue.text: Dead Roman, perhaps, or mythical Greek

indicators.note: perhaps signals the letters could be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: A question of whether a figure is a dead Roman or a figure from Greek legend.
explanation.definitionFit: Andromeda is a princess of Greek mythology, rescued by Perseus from a sea monster.

clue.text: Squandering money proves foolish with final settlement

indicators.note: foolish suggests the letters of proves are muddled

parts.note: a final settlement is an ending, the conclusion of things

explanation.surface: Wasteful spending turns out to be silly when the bill finally arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: Overspending is spending too much, a synonym for squandering money.

clue.text: Officer assisting general in plan that's crazy

indicators.note: in puts the officer inside the plan

parts.note: a map is a plan of an area
ADC, aide-de-camp, is an officer who assists a general

explanation.surface: A general's aide comes up with a scheme that's mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Madcap describes wildly impulsive behaviour, a synonym for crazy or reckless.

clue.text: Meat jelly made with a non-Eastern spice

indicators.note: non-Eastern asks for E, the abbreviation for East, to be removed from the word spice

explanation.surface: A recipe for jellied meat flavoured with a western spice.
explanation.walkthrough: E is the compass abbreviation for East.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspic is a savoury jelly made from meat stock, used to set cold dishes.

clue.text: Tenacious climber found in a variety of climates

indicators.note: a variety means a different arrangement of the letters of climates

explanation.surface: A clinging climbing plant grows in many different climates.
explanation.definitionFit: Clematis is a climbing plant that clings tenaciously to supports by its leaf stalks.

clue.text: Random attempts by snooker players?

definitions.meaning: playfully, the shots of players potting balls on a snooker table

explanation.surface: Snooker players take speculative shots at the table.
explanation.walkthrough: Snooker is a cue game in which balls are potted into pockets, so its shots are whimsically 'pot shots'.
explanation.definitionFit: A potshot is a random or opportunistic attempt, and in snooker shots pot the balls.

clue.text: Christmas present drawer

parts.note: not a drawer in a chest for storing gifts, but an animal that draws, or pulls, the sleigh full of gifts

explanation.surface: A drawer in which Christmas gifts are kept.
explanation.definitionFit: Reindeer draw, or pull, Santa's sleigh loaded with Christmas presents.

clue.text: Pub arranged to have meals in every bar

indicators.note: arranged means the letters of pub are put in a new order

parts.note: to have meals is to eat

explanation.surface: A pub is set up to serve food at every counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' shuffles the three letters of the bar. The definition is musical: every bar of music has an unaccented beat leading into the downbeat.
explanation.definitionFit: In music the unaccented beat leading into a bar's downbeat occurs in every bar.

clue.text: Was dirt-cheap? Hardly!

parts.note: dirt is soil, so being priced at the soil itself sounds cheap, but the idiom means very expensive

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at the idea that something was bargain-priced.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means was very expensive, the opposite of being dirt-cheap.

clue.text: A capital ring from one's lover

parts.note: Rome is a capital city
the letter O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: Someone receives a ring from a sweetheart in a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Romeo is Shakespeare's lover, and the name is used generally for a male lover.

clue.text: Dunce making little progress with teacher

parts.note: something making little progress is slow
a coach is a teacher or trainer

explanation.surface: A dim pupil makes little progress despite the tutor.
explanation.definitionFit: A slowcoach is a slow person, loosely a dull-witted one, akin to a dunce.

clue.text: Hotel employee has a party — and it's free!

parts.note: a reception is a formal party

indicators.note: free suggests the letters of it's are loosed into a new order

explanation.surface: A hotel worker throws a party and lets everyone in at no charge.
explanation.definitionFit: A receptionist greets guests at the front desk, a typical hotel employee.

clue.text: Model paragon, he cares for deprived children

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for the institution that does the caring

indicators.note: to model is to shape, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A model paragon of a man looks after needy children.
explanation.definitionFit: An orphanage is an institution that houses and looks after parentless children.

clue.text: Stroke of a cricketer, starting on a run?

parts.note: off means started, as when racers are off
a drive is a run out in a car

explanation.surface: A batsman's shot gets a run on the board.
explanation.walkthrough: An off drive is a cricket stroke driving the ball to the off side.
explanation.definitionFit: The off drive is a recognised cricket batting stroke, struck straight to the off side.

clue.text: Divorced ladies to be rehabilitated

indicators.note: to be rehabilitated is to be remade, so the letters are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: Divorcees are due to be brought back into normal life.
explanation.definitionFit: Divorced in the sense of cut off or separated means the same as isolated.

clue.text: Chap finds his cooked meal may be a takeaway

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters are messed about with

explanation.surface: A man discovers his supper is something bought from a takeaway shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges CHAP FINDS HIS; 'may be a takeaway' adds a hint about the meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A classic British dish of battered fried fish with chips, often bought as a takeaway meal.

clue.text: Unorthodox Easter saint

indicators.note: unorthodox means not following the usual order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A saint with an unconventional view of Easter.
explanation.definitionFit: Teresa of Avila is a Spanish saint and mystic, one of several saints with the name.

clue.text: American put up in Jack's and Paul's place

indicators.note: in puts the American inside Jack's

parts.note: a jack is a sailor, or tar, plus the possessive s

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up means the letters are written upwards

explanation.surface: An American is lodged at Jack's place and at Paul's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' turns US into SU. Saint Paul was born in Tarsus.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarsus is the city where the apostle Paul was born, his birthplace.

clue.text: A number lead the union in time-wasting action

indicators.note: lead says the number goes ahead of the union

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral 500
an alliance is a union of parties

explanation.surface: Many people head the trade union in a go-slow.
explanation.definitionFit: Dallying, or dalliance, is idle trifling that wastes time.

clue.text: Victor loses his head in the bull ring

indicators.note: losing the head means dropping the first letter of the word for victor

parts.note: the victor is the winner

explanation.surface: A champion bullfighter is beheaded in the arena.
explanation.walkthrough: The bull ring is not the bullfighting arena but the ring around the bullseye on a target.
explanation.definitionFit: On an archery or darts target the inner is the ring next to the bullseye.

clue.text: A period return for Wembley, say

indicators.note: return means the letters are read backwards

parts.note: the article a in its form an
an era is a period of history

explanation.surface: Coming back to Wembley for one period of play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns AN ERA into ARENA. Wembley is England's national football stadium in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Wembley is an example of a sports arena, England's national football stadium.

clue.text: Steadfast purpose

explanation.definitionFit: Intent as an adjective means resolved; as a noun it means aim or purpose.

clue.text: Big waves, which finally demolish old ships

definitions.meaning: heavy seas crashing on a shore
ship-... are the yards and people that dismantle retired vessels

explanation.surface: Huge seas finish off old wrecks.
explanation.definitionFit: Breakers are large waves; ship-breakers also scrap old vessels, so both are breakers.

clue.text: Last though almost sure to finish first

indicators.note: first says the finish comes at the front

parts.note: the end is the finish

indicators.note: almost means one letter of sure goes missing

explanation.surface: It will last, though it's nearly certain to finish first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops one letter, here the opening one, and 'first' puts the finish at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: To last means to go on or survive, a synonym for endure.

clue.text: Animals involved in the chase

indicators.note: involved means intricately tangled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Animals take part in the hunt.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheetahs are big cats, animals famed for chasing prey at speed.
